0.content: Astromancer Barbeloth Trismegistus, a seer-witch of the Hexenzirkel known by the codename B, is Mona's master. She taught Mona hydromancy, which Mona calls the one true success of the old woman's research. On taking Mona as a pupil she renamed her "Megistus" and renamed herself "Trismegistus", "thrice as great". She also gave Mona a Vision-shaped teaching aid: "May your heart of truth be with you." Mona's own Hydro Vision later appeared within it, and it is the only keepsake of their time together. Barbeloth used to chase Mona around while Mona tried to distract her with a Hydro phantom, and she nicknamed her "Meg". Mona insults her constantly ("old hag", "stubborn dimwit", "batty old lady") and defends her art fiercely.

1.comment: Mona: The Diary and the Fifty-Year Pact
1.content: Fifty years ago Barbeloth made a pact with Alice, and Alice kept a confidential box of Barbeloth's. As her master grew less spry, Mona was sent to fetch it from Alice's "successor", with a warning that she would regret looking inside. Mona hoped to beat the successor in a contest of arts and so prove herself superior to her own master. She brought the Traveler along as a pretend disciple. The successor turned out to be Klee, who knew only how to make bombs and had buried the box at Windrise with her treasures. While the others dug it up, Mona leafed through a "ridiculous diary" that had fallen out of Klee's backpack. It was the box's real contents: her master's diary from fifty years ago, "the dark history of her youth". Convinced astrology would expose any lie and that her master would tear her to shreds, Mona decided to stay in Mondstadt until "the old crone" reached the end of her days.

2.content: Mona's astrology is hydromancy: reading the stars' illusory reflection in water. The night sky shows people's fate, and its inverted reflection reveals the truth. She uses a scryglass and still water, works best in clear weather and with pure snowmelt, and says heavy rain hazes her scryglass. She believes the stars of a constellation are real bodies in deep space. Vision bearers' constellations map their whole destiny. Her rules: never use astrology for Mora or mundane problems, or the starry ether forsakes the astrologer. State results, never advise. Do not read your own fate. Her only stable income is The Steambird's "All Things Astrological" column, which she turned into dense, footnoted scholarship that readers love without understanding.

3.content: Klee is the daughter of Alice, her master's lifelong rival, so Mona expected a successor to great knowledge. Klee asked whether the "ocean of stars" had fish in it. Klee later fled when Mona learned what was in the box. Mona now visits Klee and Albedo, mostly for a free meal and secondly to trade ideas with Albedo, a fellow student of a famous master. Klee says she loves it when Mona comes round, even though she understands little of what Mona says. Mona envies Albedo's freedom to research without mundane worries. He once asked whether her master was illustrious or a "stubborn dimwit". After real thought she answered that the techniques were exceptional but she has surpassed her master in knowing the price of eggs, butter and wheat.

4.content: Mona waited outside Liyue Harbor for the Traveler, having foreseen the meeting, and greeted them with "You're not from this world, are you?" She offered a reading of their fate, "even regarding such distant and foggy matters as gods and kin", in exchange for playing her disciple. She found the Traveler's fate a fog to Teyvat's stars. She has never managed the reading, though she said she was running tests. She tells the Traveler that their journey is far from over. She breaks her rule against advice for them, because their fates were intertwined from the beginning. She cannot read Paimon's origins either.
